messages:
Ava (Product): Quick sync — proposing a single discovery endpoint to return model capability flags + limits. Need to agree on shape, fallback semantics, and launch criteria for beta. Thoughts?

Riley (Eng-API): ok, core questions: 1) one endpoint per model id or a catalog endpoint with variants? 2) should flags be boolean or enum? 3) include per-route hints (e.g., streaming=true) or separate profiles?

Sam (Eng-Runtime): prefer one canonical endpoint per model_id + optional /runtime-variants. Keep flags as booleans for simplest checks, but include a small "profiles" array for negotiated variants. Also need explicit max_tokens and max_input_tokens at runtime.

Jordan (ML Research): +1 to boolean flags for feature detection. Important: separate "capabilities" (what model can do) from "behaviors" (how it behaves under quantization/seq len). e.g. "functions": true but "functions_confidence":"low" could exist. Maybe a lightweight enum for confidence.

Ava (Product): Launch criteria idea: - discovery returns at least {chat, embeddings, streaming, functions, structured_output} for GA models - docs & examples for each flag - integration tests with 3 reference apps + 2 customers for Dedicated/Private. Agree?

Taylor (Support): Customers keep asking about token limits per deployment (dedicated vs hosted). We should expose both model_max_tokens and deployment_max_tokens (and which one is authoritative). Also need clear error mapping when client hits limit (HTTP 413 vs 400).

Riley (Eng-API): draft response shape suggestion:```
GET /v1/models/{model_id}/capabilities
200 OK
{
  "model_id":"redwood-7b-v2",
  "capabilities":["chat","embeddings","streaming","functions","structured_output","rerank"],
  "flags":{ "streaming": true, "functions": true, "structured_output": true },
  "limits":{ "model_max_tokens":32768, "deployment_max_tokens":30720, "max_input_tokens":30720 },
  "profiles":[{"name":"low-latency","quant":"int8","note":"reduced quality for latency"}]
}
```

Sam (Eng-Runtime): That shape looks usable. Need to add a "compat_with" map for fallback routing, e.g. if a model lacks streaming: `"compat_with":{"streaming":["redwood-7b-streaming-compat"]}` so router can pick fallback. Also include a version field for the capability schema.

Jordan (ML Research): One more: include a small test prompt ID list we use for quality gating in the discovery response metadata (not the full dataset, just keys) so clients can surface warning if their prompts are likely to regress. e.g. "regression_checks":["promptset-embed-2026-01"]

Ava (Product): For beta scope: implement endpoint + docs; expose boolean flags + limits + compat_with; implement router fallback for streaming+functions; run canary with 3 partners. GA when we have 90% pass on regression_checks and 3 months of telemetry.

Taylor (Support): Add: clear troubleshooting guide for "capability advertised but failing" cases. Also include a metric we can report to customers (capability_uptime).

Riley (Eng-API): Action items: 1) spec PR with JSON Schema + examples (I'll open today). 2) add schema versioning header X-Capabilities-Schema. 3) error contract for 404 vs 200-with-deprecated-flag.

Sam (Eng-Runtime): I’ll add runtime mapping + fallback logic in the router. Need API to call runtime to refresh cache on deployment change.

disco-bot: New doc created: https://redwood.internal/docs/discovery-api/draft-capabilities-spec (preview) :link:

Ava (Product): Great—Riley + Sam pair to delivery plan, Jordan to define regression_checks, Taylor to draft support runbook. We’ll reconvene Wednesday 11am to finalize launch criteria. :thumbsup:
